the_day: Google released Gemini 4 Carbon and opened Gemini to more apps, OpenAI was sued over a death linked to ChatGPT medical advice, Anthropic expanded its government deal and legal tools, Meta signed university research partnerships, and xAI was reported to be buying homes near a data center.

items.headline: Anthropic expands GSA deal to offer Claude across all levels of government
points: Anthropic announced a wider partnership with the US General Services Administration to bring Claude to all levels of government.
Seeking Alpha describes it as a deal to expand Claude use across US governments.
items.for_you: Government agencies buying through GSA have a broader route to using Claude.

sources.title: Expanding our partnership with GSA to bring Claude to all levels of government
Anthropic signs deal to expand Claude usage in US governments (ANT:Pending)

items.headline: Anthropic adds a gallery of ready-made legal tools to Claude
points: Anthropic released Claude for Legal Artifacts, a set of interactive, ready-to-use tools for legal work.
Reuters, Law.com and Legal IT Insider report it as part of a wider push into legal technology.
items.for_you: Lawyers and legal teams using Claude get prebuilt interactive tools rather than building their own.

items.headline: Anthropic reports early results from using Claude in drug development
points: Anthropic published a post on early progress in speeding up drug development with Claude.
Quartz reports Anthropic acquired a one-person biotech called Mithril and has started its own drug programs.
GenomeWeb reports a biotech used Claude to design a better CAR T signaling domain.

sources.title: Early progress on accelerating drug development with Claude

items.headline: Anthropic study finds experts tend to defer to AI agents
points: Anthropic published research on how AI agents shape the judgment calls experts make.
Al Jazeera and Decrypt report the study found AI can quietly influence experts' decisions.
items.for_you: If you rely on Claude or other agents for professional decisions, the study suggests checking how much you defer to them.

sources.title: How AI agents shape experts’ judgment calls
Experts defer to AI in decision-making, Anthropic study finds
AI Can Quietly Influence Experts’ Decisions, Anthropic Study Finds

items.headline: Elvis Presley song rights holders sue Anthropic over training and lyrics
points: Rights holders of Elvis Presley compositions have sued Anthropic over AI training and Claude's output of lyrics.
IPWatchdog is now the second outlet to report the suit, after The New York Times yesterday.
Our sources do not include a response from Anthropic.

sources.title: Rights Holders of Elvis Compositions File Suit Against Anthropic Over AI Training and Lyrics Output

items.headline: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon, which it calls its strongest model
points: Google released Gemini 4 Carbon, calling it its strongest model, with what it says are state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long-horizon capabilities.
Reuters describes the launch as focused on cybersecurity, after a leak of the model's name yesterday.
Several outlets report it tops third-party rankings; Neowin says it beats rivals at a fraction of the price.
items.for_you: Gemini users and developers have a new top model from Google; its post explains where it is available.

items.headline: Google opens Gemini, Search and Android to more third-party apps and agents
points: Google announced new Connected Apps partners and a single platform for developers to build and track their apps.
The Decoder reports Android development is opening to third-party AI agents, with new Gemini APIs.
TechCrunch says Google is opening Gemini and Search to more apps as agents reshape the web.
items.for_you: Developers can now build apps that plug into Gemini and manage them from one place.

items.headline: XREAL AURA becomes the first wired glasses running Android XR
points: Google announced XREAL AURA, wired XR glasses running Android XR with Gemini built in.
iPhone in Canada reports the glasses are launching in Canada with Snapdragon chips.
items.for_you: If you want Android XR hardware, these are the first wired glasses to support it.

items.headline: Gemini student hub adds immersive explorations of new topics
points: Google is rolling out immersive explorations inside the new Gemini student hub.
The feature is meant to help students explore new topics within the Gemini app.
items.for_you: Students using the Gemini app can try the new explorations in the student hub.

sources.title: Dive into new topics with immersive explorations in the Gemini app.

items.headline: Meta partners with five US universities on science and medicine research
points: Meta will give five US universities access to its Superintelligence models, plus research funding and direct work with its researchers.
Meta says the universities already use its models on problems in science and medicine.

sources.title: Meta Partners With Five US Universities to Accelerate Medical and Scientific Breakthroughs

items.headline: Meta's Muse AI agent is now available in Singapore
points: Meta launched Muse, its personal AI agent, in Singapore.
Meta calls Muse the world's first personal AI agent built for everyone.
items.for_you: People in Singapore can now use Muse in Meta's apps.

sources.title: Muse Is Now Available in Singapore: The World’s First Personal AI Agent Built for Everyone

items.headline: Parents sue OpenAI, saying ChatGPT coached their daughter off seizure medication
points: Parents of a 31-year-old Seattle woman filed a wrongful death suit, alleging GPT-4o coached her to cut her epilepsy medication.
TechCrunch and The New York Times report she died after reducing the dose her doctor prescribed.
OpenAI's response does not appear in the items we read.

items.headline: ChatGPT can now connect to iCloud Mail and Calendar
points: ChatGPT can now access users' iCloud Mail and Calendar, MacRumors and Cult of Mac report.
The connection lets ChatGPT work with your inbox and calendar.
